Large US bank stocks are under historic pressure:

The KBW Bank Index has dropped for 6 consecutive weeks, its longest streak since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

This also marks its 3rd-longest streak this century.

Over this span, the index has fallen -11%, to its lowest level since the first week of June.

Bank of America, $BAC, State Street, $STT, and Citigroup, $C, were among the worst performers over this period, declining -18%, -14%, and -10%, respectively.

This comes amid rising investor concerns over AI disrupting financial services and higher interest rate expectations.

Furthermore, mixed Q3 2026 earnings results reported last week failed to ease the pressure.

Large US bank stocks are having a terrible year.

BREAKING: Interest expense on US public debt rose +$144 billion YoY in FY2026, or +12%, to a record $1.36 trillion.

This marks the 6th consecutive annual increase, for a total of +$839 billion, or +161%.

For perspective, total receipts rose just +3.2% YoY, to $5.40 trillion.

In other words, interest on federal debt accounted for 25% of total US government receipts.

Meanwhile, Social Security, the largest government expense, jumped +$86 billion YoY, or +5.5%, to a record $1.67 trillion.

At this pace, interest costs will exceed Social Security as the largest government outlay by the end of 2028.

What is the long-term plan here?

BREAKING: US equity ETFs have attracted +$1.4 trillion in inflows over the last 12 months, their largest 12-month inflow on record.

Tech funds alone have attracted +$65 billion, more than double the inflows into cyclical equity ETFs.

At the same time, defensive equity ETFs have drawn +$25 billion.

In the preceding 12-month period, US equity ETFs attracted +$850 billion.

By comparison, during years 1 and 2 of the current bull market, inflows totaled +$300 billion and +$650 billion, respectively.

Investors are piling into US equity funds at a record pace.

And Bitcoin? A new 4-year cycle bull market could be underway, based on its power law patterns. There doesn’t seem to be a narrative, but then again, bull markets rarely start with one. https://t.co/trJJ2giWdh

BREAKING: The US deficit widened to $1.99 trillion for FY2026, up +12% from the $1.78 trillion recorded last year.

Spending rose by +6%, to $7.4 trillion, and NET interest officially rose above $1 trillion.

Debt servicing costs are now their third largest expense for the US government, only behind Social Security and Medicare.

This marks the fourth-straight year with the US fiscal deficit around $2 trillion.

The deficit spending crisis is out of control.

BREAKING: Retail investors bought +$9.1 billion of US equities last week, their largest weekly purchase over the last 16 weeks.

This also marks their 9th-largest weekly purchase over the last 12 months.

This follows purchases of +$6.4 billion in the prior week and +$4.8 billion two weeks earlier.

Semiconductors led last week's demand, attracting +$2.6 billion, the 3rd-largest weekly retail purchase over the last year.

Retail investors also bought +$2.4 billion of AI Infrastructure stocks, their 4th-largest weekly purchase over the last 12 months.

Retail investor appetite for AI-related names is surging.
